text:
Ryan Strome came to Calgary at last season's trade deadline, and tonight he sees the Rangers, the team he spent 263 games with. He's a middle-six centre in this version of his career, at about 14 minutes a night, with six points in 18 games.

The points are light, and our numbers think a good part of that is bad luck around him: the Flames have scored 6.0 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on the ice, the kind of gap that usually swings back. Calgary is about even in chances with him on the ice, and better than without him. The shooting is a mixed picture. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him shooting a lot last season (81st percentile in attempts) but not from the slot as often as that volume suggests, and only 31% of his entries were carries, which tilts his line toward dump-ins. His top speed and shot speed both sit near the bottom of the league. If the luck turns, expect something close to our 34-point median.
